lens: Security — secrets exposure, file integrity during mass move, supply-chain signature, reference coherence for security-critical specs
answer: PR #18 is a path-flatten of specs/cross-cutting/* → specs/* (95-100% git rename similarity per `git show 743a6fe6 --name-status`) plus reference updates across 222 files. No new code paths, no new attack surface, no auth/authz/IO touched. Title's 'signed replacement' refers to git commit signing (the original PR #14 contained unsigned commit f2c0696 which GitHub branch-protection rejected). Verified: the replacement commit 237a2b30 carries a Good ED25519 signature (`git verify-commit` returns 'Good "git" signature for jasonlee@bominal.com with ED25519 key SHA256:QgWf7uAizVJFJEIUCVdGg8B8TDueXC66tiVMiGIw9/U'). The trailing merge commit 743a6fe6 shows 'N' (no signature) which is GitHub web-merge default and the documented pipeline behavior, not a regression. Integrity: at merge 743a6fe6, all five sampled security-critical JSON files (specs/forbidden-operations.json, specs/masterplan.json, specs/root-hub-pointers.json, and all three .omc/handoffs/*.json) parse cleanly with `jq -e`; the old `specs/cross-cutting/forbidden-operations.json` path returns 'fatal: path … does not exist in 743a6fe6', proving the rename is atomic with no duplicate/orphan blobs. Reference coherence: 18 of 18 in-diff references to /specs/cross-cutting/forbidden-operations.json and /specs/cross-cutting/decision-principles.json were rewritten to the flat /specs/ path in the SAME commit (IP-001..IP-006 multi-subscription-pool plans, all six call-sites), so security-doctrine pointers stay resolvable. Secrets: zero hits scanning the diff and the .omc/handoffs/, .omc/plans/milestones/M02-foundry-preview/phases/P02-multi-subscription-pool/ (which contains the OAuth subscription capture plan) trees for AKIA*, ghp_*, sk_live, BEGIN PRIVATE KEY, JWT eyJ.eyJ, bearer-tokens, or client_secret literals — the IP-004-oauth-subscription-capture.md is a planning document describing the OAuth flow, never an artifact storing live tokens. Tenant config: none — the M03-first-tenant INDEX.md edit is a single-line path-pointer rewrite, no tenant payloads in scope.
key_claims: Replacement commit 237a2b30 is GPG/SSH-signed (Good ED25519 signature jasonlee@bominal.com); the 'signed replacement' title is verifiably accurate vs PR #14's unsigned ancestor f2c0696.

Trailing merge commit 743a6fe6 is unsigned ('N') — this is GitHub web-merge default and matches the pipeline's documented behavior; the authored replacement commit (which carries the actual tree change) IS signed, so the PR-level claim holds.

Atomic rename: `git show 743a6fe6 --name-status` reports R094-R100 similarity for every specs/cross-cutting/X → specs/X pair, including security-critical forbidden-operations.json (R095) and decision-principles.json (R094); no add/delete pairs that would indicate content corruption.

Post-merge integrity: forbidden-operations.json, masterplan.json, root-hub-pointers.json, and all three .omc/handoffs/*.json files parse with `jq -e .` at merge commit 743a6fe6; $id field in forbidden-operations.json correctly updated to https://docs.oyatie.dev/specs/forbidden-operations.json (drops /cross-cutting/ segment in lockstep with the path move).

Reference coherence verified for every in-diff occurrence: all 18 in-diff references to forbidden-operations.json and decision-principles.json (IP-001..IP-006 multi-subscription-pool plans) rewritten in the SAME commit; no dangling /specs/cross-cutting/ references survive in tracked files at merge.

Secrets scan: zero hits across the diff and the live .omc/handoffs/ + P02-multi-subscription-pool/ trees for AKIA*, ghp_*, sk_live, BEGIN PRIVATE KEY, JWT, bearer-tokens, client_secret literals. IP-004-oauth-subscription-capture.md is a planning document, not a capture artifact.
No tenant config, no OAuth captures, no TLS material, no credential blobs touched; PR #18 surface is pure path topology + reference rewrite.
uncertainty_areas: Reviewer cannot independently verify the SSH signing key's provenance vs GitHub allowed_signers without admin access to the org's signing-key registry; trust is delegated to branch-protection's signed-commits gate.

Reviewer scanned the in-diff hunks and the live post-merge subset of touched directories; an exhaustive scan of all 222 modified files for secret-like regex was not performed (sampling-based confidence). Probability of missed secret is low because the file types are .md/.json planning artifacts, not code.

Whether downstream consumers outside the modified 222-file set (e.g., out-of-repo CI scripts, external Argo Applications, agent prompt templates cached elsewhere) still resolve to /specs/cross-cutting/ — only in-repo references were checked; HEAD on the reviewer's working branch still uses /specs/cross-cutting/ paths because this branch forked before PR #18 merged, which is expected and not a PR #18 defect.
anti_patterns_detected: Trailing merge commit is unsigned ('N'). Acceptable for GitHub web-merge convention and matches the rest of the recent merge history (e.g., merge of PR #5/#6/#13/#15 all show similar pattern), but worth tracking in policy: if branch-protection ever escalates to require signatures on merge commits as well, the GitHub web-UI merge path will break.

findings.summary: Merge commit 743a6fe6 is unsigned ('N' per `git verify-commit`); only the authored replacement commit 237a2b30 carries the ED25519 signature.
findings.recommended_action: No action this PR. Track for future ADR-0083 (signed-history policy): if signatures become required on merge commits, switch to API-merge with --merge-method=rebase or use a signed-merge bot. Current posture matches the documented GitHub web-merge convention.

findings.summary: $id field in moved JSON schemas (e.g., forbidden-operations.json) updated in lockstep with path move, which is correct, but no automated CI lane currently validates $id↔path coherence after future moves.
findings.recommended_action: Out-of-scope for PR #18. Track as a fitness lane proposal: a single-grep check `jq -r '."$id"' specs/*.json | grep -v $(basename …)` to fail CI on drift between $id and on-disk path. Low priority — this PR did it correctly by hand.

findings.summary: IP-004-oauth-subscription-capture.md (planning doc) was modified by the PR; reviewer confirmed it contains no captured tokens, only flow descriptions, but the file's name pattern triggers naive secret-scanners.
findings.recommended_action: No action. Flagged so future reviewers do not assume the .md is a capture artifact. The actual capture path (when implemented) must land secret material in OpenBao per ADR-0043, never in a tracked .md.
